speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are experiencing shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and a large ovarian mass. To help narrow down the cause, is the abdominal swelling accompanied by a sensation of fullness or early satiety when eating?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Have you noticed any unintended weight loss, pelvic pain, or changes in your bowel habits like constipation or diarrhea?
I would also like to check for ascites and palpable lymph nodes during a physical examination.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Shortness of breath. I also have Increased abdominal girth, Fatigue, No significant weight loss or gain.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the rapid onset of symptoms, I need to know if you are experiencing any pelvic pain or pressure, and whether you have noticed any vaginal bleeding or discharge. I will now request a pelvic ultrasound and a CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis to evaluate the ovarian mass and check for ascites.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, does not consume alcohol regularly. Works as a high school teacher.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is highly unusual for a large ovarian mass to yield completely normal imaging results. Have you noticed any swelling in your legs or ankles, and do you feel full quickly after starting a meal?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, night sweats, chest pain, or swelling in the legs. She has not noticed any changes in bowel or urinary habits.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the normal imaging and lack of typical malignant signs, I suspect Meigs syndrome, where an ovarian fibroma causes ascites and pleural effusion. To confirm this, I need to evaluate your lung bases for fluid accumulation.

REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray
REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest X-Ray: Right-sided pleural effusion; Echocardiogram: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of a right-sided pleural effusion alongside the ovarian mass and ascites, with a normal heart, strongly supports Meigs syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Meigs syndrome
